scanlines_per_frame.resolving_evidence: pending: a tier 1 to 3 source for lines per frame, or a measurement

scanlines_per_frame.note: A nominal frame is 14,934 CPU cycles = 59,736 master ticks. A frame is a timeline event and is never derived by modulo.

cpu_cycles_per_scanline.resolving_evidence: pending: a tier 1 to 3 source for cycles per line, or a measurement

reset.r7.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 SC.1, pdf 21 and pdf 27 (the start PC is device-supplied over the bus by IAB); SRC-community-emu-docs for the $1000 default
reset.r7.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 reset read-back on owner hardware (D5 decided as D-24: user-supplied system images only; project boot stub in Phase 4)
reset.r7.note: The manual says the start PC is supplied by a device through the bus via IAB. Whether the EXEC or the board supplies it is unknown-default-chosen; D5 decided as D-24 (user-supplied images only, project boot stub in Phase 4), so the EXEC or the boot stub supplies it.

reset.registers_other.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 SC.1, pdf 21: other registers are undefined at reset; zero is the chosen default
reset.registers_other.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 reset read-back on owner hardware
reset.registers_other.revisit_trigger: when a source documents the reset state or a hardware read-back exists

reset.flags.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 SC.1, pdf 21: flags are undefined at reset; zero is the chosen default
reset.flags.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 reset read-back on owner hardware
reset.flags.revisit_trigger: when a source documents the reset state or a hardware read-back exists

interrupt.iab_value.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22 (the interrupt vector is supplied over the bus by the IAB access); SRC-community-emu-docs for the $1004 value
interrupt.iab_value.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 interrupt vector read-back on owner hardware
interrupt.iab_value.revisit_trigger: when a source documents the interrupt vector or a hardware read-back exists
interrupt.iab_value.note: The core holds no vector constant. The machine bus answers the IAB access with this value for an interrupt, as reset.r7 is answered for a reset.

cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22, pdf 56: the pages do not say that accepting an interrupt clears the interrupt enable; not-cleared is the chosen default
cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 repeated-interrupt probe on owner hardware
cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff.revisit_trigger: when a source documents the enable state after acceptance or a hardware probe exists
cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff.note: 0 = false, 1 = true. Stored as a number because the profile schema has no boolean value type.

bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 36: the bus request timing diagram, read as a 2 CPU cycle release latency
bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 bus trace on owner hardware
bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: when a bus trace exists or the Phase 6 STIC bus-request timing depends on it

bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles.cite: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 12, pdf 40, pdf 43: a device must answer in under 40 microseconds; 35 CPU cycles is the derived cap
bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 slow-device probe on owner hardware
bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles.revisit_trigger: when a bus trace exists or a device needs a longer hold

cartridge.slots.value: one slot, ROM-only 10-bit decles; no bank switching, cartridge RAM, ECS or IntelliVoice
cartridge.slots.cite: none: scope choice for the first profile (D3)
cartridge.slots.revisit_trigger: when a content profile needs bank switching, cartridge RAM, ECS or IntelliVoice

cartridge.features_supported.cite: none: project cartridge format IVSC v1 (D-29, D-32); required_features is a u32 mask and v1 defines no bit
cartridge.features_supported.revisit_trigger: when a cartridge format version defines a feature bit
cartridge.features_supported.note: A cartridge whose required_features has a bit outside this mask is refused UNSUPPORTED (D-32).

system_images.exec_grom.value: user-supplied only: no built-in, fetched or high-level-emulated image (D-24); the Phase 4 project boot stub loads through the EXEC slot and is labelled "project boot stub, not an EXEC"
system_images.exec_grom.cite: none: rights policy (AGENTS.md, docs/RIGHTS.md); system images are never committed or redistributed
system_images.exec_grom.revisit_trigger: when the owner wants plug-and-play commercial play (a separately labelled high-level image) or permission to redistribute an image appears
system_images.exec_grom.note: Slot shapes are system_images.exec and system_images.grom. Identity is a recorded fact: the core checks shape only (D-27).

system_images.exec.cite: SRC-bsr-2609 for the 4K EXEC size; SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13 (pdf 194) for the 10-bit words; SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847) for the $1000 base
system_images.exec.revisit_trigger: when board evidence places the EXEC halves (C20) or D11 checks a real image
system_images.exec.decision: D-24 and D-26 (delegated decision, phase 3 context)
system_images.exec.note: Raw container: 8192 bytes, 4096 words high byte first, bits 15..10 zero (D-26). Required: a power-on reset with this slot empty is refused MISSING_SYSTEM_IMAGE (D-14).

system_images.grom.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-16 (pdf 197): RO-3-9503 is 2048 x 8 and sits at $3000-$37FF after an SR1 pulse
system_images.grom.revisit_trigger: when D11 checks a real image
system_images.grom.decision: D-24 and D-26 (delegated decision, phase 3 context)
system_images.grom.note: Raw container: exactly 2048 bytes (D-26). Required: a power-on reset with this slot empty is refused MISSING_SYSTEM_IMAGE (D-14).

memmap.undriven_read.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847): reads of undriven space return $FFFF, bus pull-ups being the likely mechanism; no tier 1 to 3 source found
memmap.undriven_read.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 read-back of undriven addresses on owner hardware
memmap.undriven_read.revisit_trigger: when a source documents undriven reads or a hardware read-back exists
memmap.undriven_read.note: Also the read value of a closed gate and of an EXEC, GROM or cartridge region with no image loaded (D-17, D-19). Never $0000: decle $0000 is HLT.

memmap.device.rom10.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13 (pdf 194: the RO-3-9502 outputs 10 data bits and drives logic zero on the top six bits) and printed 5-21 (pdf 202: the RO-3-9504 drives the higher 6 bits to zero on reads)
memmap.device.rom10.revisit_trigger: when content on a non-GI ROM part is in scope
memmap.device.rom10.note: read = (stored & rmask) | (fill & ~rmask) (D-17). The fill is a driven zero, not the undriven pull-up value. Bus stores are dropped; loaders refuse a word above $03FF instead of masking it.

memmap.device.grom8.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-16 (pdf 197): the RO-3-9503 has an 8 bit tri-state bus with the higher 8 bits driven to zero during reads
memmap.device.grom8.revisit_trigger: when a GROM device engine replaces the plain read (Phase 5 or later)
memmap.device.grom8.note: Bus stores are dropped; the GROM is read-only.

memmap.device.ram16.cite: SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-18 (pdf 199): the RA-3-9600 is 352 x 16; the two most significant bits are available for user storage
memmap.device.ram16.revisit_trigger: when a hardware read-back contradicts a full-width store
memmap.device.ram16.note: Stores and reads keep all 16 bits.

memmap.device.ram8.cite: SRC-bsr-2609 for the 8-bit scratchpad and GRAM parts; none-found for what bits 15..8 read as
memmap.device.ram8.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 read-back of scratchpad and GRAM reads on owner hardware
memmap.device.ram8.revisit_trigger: when a source documents the upper byte of 8-bit RAM reads or a hardware read-back exists
memmap.device.ram8.note: Stores keep value & $00FF; reads give the stored byte with bits 15..8 zero.

memmap.device.stub.cite: none-found: no source documents STIC or PSG register reads for a device the core does not implement yet
memmap.device.stub.resolving_evidence: measurement: D10 read-back of STIC and PSG register reads on owner hardware
memmap.device.stub.revisit_trigger: when the PSG phase (5) or the STIC phase (6) implements the device
memmap.device.stub.note: A stub region is decoded and named but holds no state: reads give the undriven value and writes are dropped (D-19).

memmap.region.exec.cite: SRC-intv-wiki (Memory Map, oldid 14847) for $1000-$1FFF; SRC-bsr-2609 for the 4K EXEC size; SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13 (pdf 194) for the 2048 x 10 part with a mask-programmed 2K page location

input.controllers.cite: SRC-bsr-2609 (two hand controllers, each on one of the sound chip's two 8-bit I/O ports); research-era reading, not re-read in phase 4

input.controllers.note: connected hand controllers; event word index = PSG port (0 = R14, 1 = R15); no Phase 4 consumer. A nonzero controller word at an index at or above this value is refused UNSUPPORTED (D-13, D-15, plan 04-12).
